record.paper_title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density
record.original_question: In electron-nucleus diffractive vector-meson production or deeply virtual Compton scattering, can the incoherent diffractive background from nuclear breakup be removed efficiently enough to access the first minimum and maximum of the momentum-transfer distribution, thereby enabling extraction of transverse spatial distributions and correlations of partons from the t dependence of the cross section?

evidence.quote: Diffractive vector meson production (or deeply virtual Compton scattering when the produced vector particle is a photon) is pictured in Fig. 7 (left). This exclusive process provides access to the spatial distributions (and correlations) of partons in the transverse plane, unlike the more inclusive processes discussed before. Indeed, this information can be obtained through a Fourier transformation of the t dependence of the cross section, where t is the square of the momentum transferred by the target.

Coming back to the momentum transfer dependence, Fig. 8 shows diffractive J/Ψ and φ production off a gold nucleus. Depending on how efficiently the incoherent background can be removed (incoherent diffraction allows the possible break-up of the target nucleus into its constituent nucleons), one could access the first minimum and maximum of the distribution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider exclusive diffractive vector-meson production (e.g., J/ψ or φ) and deeply virtual Compton scattering in electron–nucleus scattering, e + A → e + V + A' (or e + A → e + γ + A'), where the squared momentum transfer to the nuclear target is t. The coherent component of the cross section dσ/dt (in which the nucleus remains intact) carries, via Fourier transform with respect to √|t|, information about the transverse spatial distribution and correlations of partons (in particular gluons) inside the nucleus. The coherent dσ/dt exhibits diffractive structure with successive minima and maxima at characteristic values of |t|. The incoherent component, in which the nucleus breaks up into its constituent nucleons (and possibly nuclear fragments), constitutes a large background that, in the relevant range of |t|, can dominate over the coherent signal—especially around the first diffractive minimum.

Question: For a heavy nuclear target such as gold, can the incoherent diffractive background associated with nuclear breakup be experimentally rejected (e.g., by vetoing emitted nucleons, nuclear fragments, and photons in the forward region, combined with realistic detector resolution and |t| smearing) with sufficiently high efficiency that the coherent dσ/dt can be measured cleanly through at least its first diffractive minimum and the subsequent first maximum, thereby enabling the extraction of transverse spatial distributions and correlations of partons from the t dependence of the cross section?
artifact.category_tag: Diffractive imaging in QCD / Electron-Ion Collider
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent EIC simulation studies (Tu, Jentsch, et al., Phys. Rev. D 104, 114030 (2021), arXiv:2108.01694) show that with the proposed EIC far-forward detector design and BeAGLE-based veto on nuclear breakup products, the incoherent background can be suppressed with vetoing efficiencies of roughly 80–99% depending on |t|, sufficient to expose the coherent dσ/dt at least through its first diffractive minimum after realistic |t|-smearing. Reaching deeper structures (subsequent maxima) remains more challenging, so the question is partially answered affirmatively for the first minimum/maximum, pending experimental confirmation at the EIC.

status_evidence.title: Investigation of the background in coherent J/ψ production at the EIC
status_evidence.snippet: Vetoing efficiency ranges from about 80% to 99% depending on |t|; with 5% smearing on reconstructed |t|, the efficiency suppresses the incoherent background to at least the first minimum of the coherent |t| distribution.
status_evidence.claim: Simulation studies show feasible suppression of incoherent breakup background past the first coherent diffractive minimum at the EIC.

status_evidence.title: Investigation of the background in coherent J/ψ production at the EIC — Phys. Rev. D 104, 114030
status_evidence.snippet: Peer-reviewed publication establishing the veto strategy and quantitative reach in |t| using the EIC far-forward design.
status_evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed evidence that incoherent background rejection is sufficient for accessing the coherent first diffractive minimum.
